name: Khanate
label: Hydra Head
lede: Alan Dubin screams over riffs played at a crawl, in a band put together from OLD, Burning Witch, Sunn O))) and Blind Idiot God. Khanate makes four albums by 2009, goes quiet, then releases a fifth in 2023 with no warning.

eras.title: Jersey City, at a crawl
eras.text: Two OLD veterans, a Seattle doom guitarist who has moved to New York and a jazz-trained drummer start improvising at absurd volume and glacial speed. By the end of 2001 they have a debut on Southern Lord Records built from edited jams.

years.cap: Khanate at Great Scott, Boston: Stephen O'Malley's guitar and Alan Dubin at right
years.src: CLRVYNT · The Quietus · Dead End Follies
years.h: James Plotkin meets Stephen O'Malley at an Isis show at Brownies
years.p: [[James Plotkin|d5fc2614-ce13-4d96-8e33-c855cd8eb3f3]] introduces [[Stephen O'Malley|d2db31eb-4469-4e8d-8ed2-b3c1bfff0c17]] to his old bandmate [[Alan Dubin|482f7f7b-9ccf-440f-9e84-f64da9e7351f]] and to drummer [[Tim Wyskida|321b3f6e-b1e7-4d07-9bdd-324d8caf76d0]], and the four start rehearsing in Wyskida's Jersey City space.
years.xp:
Plotkin and Dubin had met in New Jersey as teenagers and made grindcore together in [[OLD|2a7e17f0-dc67-4902-ad4b-20bd986e847b]]. O'Malley, previously of [[Burning Witch|e5d4491d-1496-4efa-a5b9-e7be001b9f6a]] and by then a co-founder of [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]], had moved to New York and was working a Midtown advertising job. Wyskida, of [[Blind Idiot God|3165e9a0-c313-47ac-ab99-f36834365e9b]], came up through jazz training.

The band's own account has the first meeting at an Isis show at the East Village club Brownies, while Dubin dates it to 2000. Dubin told Dead End Follies the rehearsals started with discipline: "We had to rehearse a lot at first to get the cues down."

O'Malley later told The Quietus the band was first going to be called Ögedi, after Genghis Khan's son, before Khanate won out.

years.h: The tektonikdoom CDR goes out in twenty copies, on yellow vellum
years.p: It predates any label deal: a 20-copy CDR demo called tektonikdoom, pressed by the band.

years.h: The debut lands on Southern Lord as SUNN14
years.p: Five tracks and 56 minutes, opening with the 13-minute "Pieces of Quiet" and ending on "No Joy". Julian Cope reviewed it in March 2002.
years.xp:
It was recorded in Wyskida's rehearsal space on a digital 8-track, then assembled by Plotkin in Cubase from riffs and edited improvisations. Plotkin told CLRVYNT the hard drive kept stopping during tracking because of the volume and the bass; O'Malley says the computer was wrapped in foam and a speaker cabinet to keep it alive.

Dubin sang so hard that, in O'Malley's telling, he lost his breath and passed out. "It was really fucking hot in there," Dubin told The Quietus. "I actually passed out a few times."

Southern Lord Records issued it as SUNN14. "Skin Coat" and "Under Rotting Sky" were written first; much of the rest was cut together from jams.

eras.title: The $666 record
eras.text: A live radio set, a borrowed 16-track and a $666 budget produce Things Viral, made with real heat between the players.

years.cap: Tim Wyskida behind the kit at Great Scott, Boston, April 3, 2002
years.h: WFMU puts the band on the air
years.p: A live set for freeform station WFMU, later issued as Live WFMU 91.1, became one of Khanate's first live documents.

years.h: Southern Lord's $666 budget buys a few microphones
years.p: [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]] of Southern Lord Records gave the band $666, and a Roland 16-track came on loan from [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] of Hydra Head Records.
years.xp:
Plotkin told CLRVYNT that Anderson handed over the $666 "as some sort of stupid joke". "So, we bought a few mics, and that was our budget."

The sessions took place in Andy Hawkins' loft in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, above a tire shop. Hawkins plays in [[Blind Idiot God|3165e9a0-c313-47ac-ab99-f36834365e9b]] with Wyskida. O'Malley switched to a Travis Bean guitar around then and says that once it arrived, "the whole band changed."

The Quietus quotes O'Malley on the room: "There was some heat between the players, and it comes across in the music." He also called the loft scene devoted but desperate.

years.cap: Alan Dubin at Great Scott, Boston
yt: Live at the Rescue Rooms, Nottingham, 2004
years.p: It closes with "Too Close Enough to Touch". Pitchfork gave it 8.2, and the band made a video for "Dead".
years.xp: James Plotkin produced, recorded and mixed it, and plays bass plus keyboards and synths. It came out as a European digipack, a U.S. jewelcase CD, and a 1,000-copy gatefold LP on Load Records. Plotkin describes it as an album about space and decay.

years.h: No Joy gets a remix EP
years.p: Southern Lord follows the album with a remix EP built around the debut's closing track, "No Joy".

eras.title: Capture, release, quit
eras.text: The band tours hard, especially in Europe, and moves from edited jams to songs worked out in the rehearsal room. Schedules and a lot of personal friction end it in the autumn of 2006.

years.h: A Stockholm set at Debaser becomes KHNT vs. Stockholm
years.p: The tour behind Things Viral also produces Let Loose the Lambs, a tour DVD limited to 230 copies.
years.xp:
Things Viral drew a particularly strong reception in Europe, and audiences there went well beyond the usual metal crowd, according to Plotkin and O'Malley in the CLRVYNT oral history. O'Malley says the shows were about the performance itself, since anything could go wrong at that tempo.

The Stockholm set was recorded at Debaser on May 13, 2004.

yt: Live at The Hook, Brooklyn, Sept 17, 2005
years.h: Day three of four booked, Capture & Release is done
years.p: Two tracks on Hydra Head Records (HH666-87): "Capture" runs 18 minutes and "Release" 25.
years.xp:
Recorded at Seizures Palace in Brooklyn with engineer [[Martin Bisi|cc9c5e4f-72dc-4525-8abd-63ba3d2b1a5b]], it was the band's first album on tape, and tracking finished on day three of four booked days. The songs were worked out together in rehearsal rather than assembled on a computer. O'Malley and Wyskida drove the writing, and Plotkin says he felt sidelined.

Mixing was its own problem. "The kick drum was going so steadily that it sounded like a 10-minute blast beat," Plotkin said. Pitchfork gave the record 7.7.

years.h: Twenty or so people turn up at the Drunken Unicorn in Atlanta
years.p: On the fall 2005 tour behind Capture & Release the band plays the Drunken Unicorn to a small crowd.
years.xp: The writer in CLRVYNT's oral history counted maybe 20 people milling about, and says Khanate stole the show anyway.

yt: Live at Great Scott, Boston, Sept 18, 2005
years.h: A DVD and a 500-copy live album arrive in the same year
years.p: Dead/Live Aktions is the DVD; It's Cold When Birds Fall from the Sky is the limited live album, 500 copies.

years.cap: Stephen O'Malley playing with Gravetemple Trio, Israel, July 2006
q: everyone was a total dick in their own individual way
years.h: James Plotkin leaves after a summer of Sunn O))) touring
years.p: After a six-week Sunn O))) run, [[Stephen O'Malley|d2db31eb-4469-4e8d-8ed2-b3c1bfff0c17]] asks for a break, then Sunn O))) takes a Celtic Frost support tour. On September 24, 2006, [[James Plotkin|d5fc2614-ce13-4d96-8e33-c855cd8eb3f3]] announces he is out.
years.xp:
Plotkin cited a lack of commitment from certain members. In a November 17 follow-up he pointed to Alan Dubin's TV commercial editing job as an obstacle to rehearsing, recording and touring, and said O'Malley's casual attitude compounded it. "If I can't be involved in writing one of my own band's records, what's the point?" he told CLRVYNT.

O'Malley says he came back from that spring 2006 tour with his personal life a mess and asked for time off. Wyskida told CLRVYNT that O'Malley putting Sunn O))) first, plus "a lot of tension around the creative process and money issues," ended the band.

eras.title: Other bands, one more album, no reunion
eras.text: The members scatter into other groups, and in 2009 a fourth album built from unused tape appears. Festival offers arrive and go nowhere. In 2016 a compilation session puts them back in the same room.

years.cap: Stephen O'Malley with Sunn O))) at Quart Festival
years.h: After Khanate, Dubin starts Gnaw and O'Malley moves to Paris
years.p: [[James Plotkin|d5fc2614-ce13-4d96-8e33-c855cd8eb3f3]] and [[Tim Wyskida|321b3f6e-b1e7-4d07-9bdd-324d8caf76d0]] form [[Khlyst|dbae5f36-c626-426b-bb6b-d4de8289c2a3]] and [[Jodis|6064aabc-7cbf-473c-98d7-ba1eb17afa21]] (with [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]]), [[Alan Dubin|482f7f7b-9ccf-440f-9e84-f64da9e7351f]] starts [[Gnaw|cd349e0b-5b88-4e70-8f41-7582ffdbe723]], and [[Stephen O'Malley|d2db31eb-4469-4e8d-8ed2-b3c1bfff0c17]] keeps [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]] going.

years.h: A fourth album, Clean Hands Go Foul, appears after the split
years.p: Four tracks and 60 minutes on Hydra Head Records; the last runs nearly 33 minutes. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the recording to sessions in 2005, 2006 and 2008 at Seizures Palace. Wyskida told CLRVYNT it came from leftover tape from the Capture & Release session, mostly improvisations with little editing, which Plotkin rediscovered years later and Dubin sang over.

years.h: Offers from festivals arrive and go nowhere
years.p: Promoters come calling after Clean Hands Go Foul, but the talks fall through. O'Malley says writing riffs got hard after Khanate.
years.xp: The CLRVYNT oral history lists logistics and unwanted afternoon open-air slots among the reasons. Wyskida told the site, "It's unlikely we'll ever play again," and added that if everyone was ever ready, the band could give the music community "a much-needed kick."

years.h: A Drag City compilation session puts them back in a room
years.p: The band records for a Drag City compilation, and Wyskida says they realized they wanted to do more together.

years.h: Hydra Head puts Things Viral back out on silver vinyl
years.p: A limited 500-copy deluxe gatefold 2xLP on silver vinyl appears in 2016.

eras.title: To Be Cruel
eras.text: The band quietly gets back to work in 2017, then drops a surprise album on Sacred Bones in 2023.

years.cap: Stephen O'Malley with his Travis Bean 1000A guitar, August 2017
years.p: Khanate begins writing again in between other projects, and does not announce it for years.
years.xp:
SPIN reports the record that became To Be Cruel had been in the works since 2017, when the band quietly reunited and worked on it between their main projects.

Dubin told Dead End Follies it started with O'Malley and Wyskida jamming together in Europe and coming back with material.

yt: Live at Le Poisson Rouge, New York, June 3, 2025
years.h: To Be Cruel arrives with no warning, 14 years on
years.p: Khanate's first album since 2009 drops digitally on Sacred Bones Records on May 19, with physical copies on June 30.
years.xp:
It was recorded at Orgone studio in Woburn, England, which O'Malley describes as a WWII radio building that broadcast fake German radio into occupied France. Dubin described the album as portraying a self-immolating destiny that perhaps ironically blames outside entities.

SPIN notes Plotkin's subtle synths and Wyskida's sheet-metal percussion. Digital reissues of the four earlier albums were announced at the same time, with physical reissues to follow.
